author: Mark Atwood
text:
Scope clarification + recommendation after investigation.

The bead's recommendation listed three options. Option 1 (inject _new_id into created_obj before serialization) requires a setter on the concrete type. Option 2 (debug_assert!(created_obj.id() == Some(&new_id))) as written assumes the SetObject trait exposes id(). It does not — SetObject in jmap-types/src/backend.rs:29 is a pure marker trait with only a Patch associated type. Generic id-equality assertions therefore require either:
  (a) adding fn id(&self) -> Option<&Id> to SetObject in jmap-types (foundation-API addition; ripples through every concrete impl: Metadata, Email, Mailbox, Identity, Submission, Vacation, Chat, Message, Space, Calendar, CalendarEvent, Task, TaskList, Contact, FileNode, Sieve, etc. — every Set-capable type in the workspace).
  (b) per-concrete-type assertion at each call site: debug_assert!(created_obj.id() == Some(&_server_id), "..."). Each concrete type (Metadata, Email, Mailbox, etc.) already has its own id() accessor.

Workspace-wide scope of the underlying gap (verified): the canonical mail-server has the same gap at five /set create sites — email.rs:1156 (has debug_assert! for blobId only, NOT for id), mailbox.rs:602, identity.rs:266, submission.rs:930, vacation.rs:224. Per canonical-template propagation rule, mail-server must be fixed first, then propagated to chat-server, calendars-server, tasks-server, contacts-server, filenode-server, metadata-server, sharing-server.

Recommendation: option (b) — per-concrete-type debug_assert! at each call site.
  Reasons:
    - Matches the existing canonical pattern at email.rs:1158 (debug_assert! for the blobId contract); same shape, new contract.
    - Zero foundation-API change. SetObject stays a marker trait.
    - debug_assert! is the right tool: contract tripwire in dev/test, free in release builds. The contract is internal-to-the-handler; production callers should never trigger it.
    - Propagation is mechanical (one line per /set create site) and trivially reviewable.

Decision needed from human:
  (1) Accept option (b) and file children under JMAP-ayoz.28 for the 8-crate sweep (mail-server first per canonical-template rule).
  (2) Pursue option (a) — add SetObject::id() in jmap-types and use a generic assertion. Larger blast radius, but a single assertion site per handler.
  (3) Close as wontfix — P3 defensive defended by the existing 'create_object guarantees created_obj.id == server_id' comments + sibling backend conformance tests; not worth the workspace-wide sweep.
  (4) Something else.

My vote: (1). The bead's recommendation paragraph mentioned both injection and debug_assert! as alternatives, so I do not believe I'm bikeshedding a settled call — the trait-shape constraint genuinely changes which option is implementable as-stated.
